questions.evidence:
After walking beside a field, Mira finds several small hooked seeds attached to her socks. For a classroom demonstration, she brings collected seeds and three equal-size surfaces: wool cloth, smooth plastic, and plain paper. She does not collect new seeds from the protected school garden.

The class gently presses ten seeds against each surface once, then lifts the surface. Seven remain on the wool, one on the plastic, and two on the paper. Students count only seeds still attached after the surface is held upright for ten seconds.

One student says the test proves every seed travels on wool. Mira points to the hooked seeds in their sample. They have not tested other shapes, and the pressing method is only a simple demonstration, not a record of every trip through a field.

The class draws the hooks and the cloth fibers they can see. They suggest that these features help explain this result, while leaving room for another test. Their report names both the sample and the procedure so another group can try the same activity.
questions.explanation: 樣本、程序與結果都清楚才便於比較與重複。
options: It replaces all counts with a universal claim.
It assumes every material behaves like wool.
It hides how long surfaces were held upright.
It describes the sample and method along with the results.
questions.prompt: What makes the report useful to another group?

lessons.story:
After walking beside a field, Mira finds several small hooked seeds attached to her socks. For a classroom demonstration, she brings collected seeds and three equal-size surfaces: wool cloth, smooth plastic, and plain paper. She does not collect new seeds from the protected school garden.

The class gently presses ten seeds against each surface once, then lifts the surface. Seven remain on the wool, one on the plastic, and two on the paper. Students count only seeds still attached after the surface is held upright for ten seconds.

One student says the test proves every seed travels on wool. Mira points to the hooked seeds in their sample. They have not tested other shapes, and the pressing method is only a simple demonstration, not a record of every trip through a field.

The class draws the hooks and the cloth fibers they can see. They suggest that these features help explain this result, while leaving room for another test. Their report names both the sample and the procedure so another group can try the same activity.
